chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who claimed upon a woman that he had married her with a guardian and witnesses, and the woman denied that. So the sister of this woman established the proof upon this man that he had married her with a guardian and witnesses, but they did not specify a time. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The proof is the proof of the man, and the proof of the woman is not acceptable because the husband has established his right to the conjugal relations of this woman, and her sister wants the invalidation of the marriage. And it is not ratified, nor is her proof acceptable except with a time before her time, or with his entering (consummation) with her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a woman denies marriage but her sister provides evidence with a man who claims he married her with witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'presumption of validity' (istishab) in marital disputes, where the husband's claim prevails unless the wife or her representative can prove the marriage was defective or non-existent. The ruling emphasizes that a woman's testimony alone is insufficient to overturn the husband's established right to conjugal relations (bush') without corroborating evidence of timing or consummation, reflecting the procedural rigor of Imami fiqh in protecting familial integrity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood, from Isa Bin Yunus, from Al Awzaie, from Al Zuhry, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who claimed upon a woman that he had married with (approval of) a guardian and witnesses, and the woman denied that. So the sister of this woman established the proof upon this man that he had married her with (approval of) a guardian and witnesses, but could not determine the timing of it. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘The (admissible) proof is the proof of the man, and the proof of the woman is not acceptable because the husband is more rightful with conjugal relations with this woman, and her sister wants the spoiling of the marriage and should not be ratified, nor would her proof be acceptable with a timing before her time, or (before) he had copulated with her’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad al-Qasaniy from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud, ‘Isa ibn Yunus from al-Awza’iy from al-Zuhriy who has said the following: “About

the case of a man who claims to have married a woman in the presence of witnesses and her guardian but she denies it and the sister of this woman presents testimony that the man has married her in the presence of witnesses and her guardian but she does not prove the time of marriage. Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, issued a judgment in this case that said, ‘The testimony of the man is admitted and accepted and the testimony of the woman is not accepted because the husband is entitled to claim his conjugal right and her sister wants to destroy such right so she must not be taken as truthful and her testimony is unacceptable without specifying the time before her time or proof of consummation of marriage (the couple’s going to bed).”’
